key_insight: A neural surrogate of NGSpice helps fit transistor-model parameters to measured SKY130 behavior at 77 K. The approach connects machine-learning-assisted calibration with compact models used in standard circuit simulators.
problem_solved: Cryogenic circuit design needs transistor models that match low-temperature measurements while remaining compatible with standard simulation tools.
method: Fit BSIM4 compact-model parameters to measured SKY130 transistor current–voltage curves at 77 K.
Use a neural surrogate to map model parameters and device geometry to output and transfer characteristics.
Perform bounded least-squares parameter extraction, supported by a bank of NGSpice simulations.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this illustrates how surrogate models can support calibration of physics-based simulators. It targets cryogenic electronics modeling, though the supplied abstract excerpt provides no quantitative accuracy or speedup results.
visual_elements: Workflow: NGSpice simulation bank → neural surrogate → parameter fitting → calibrated BSIM4 model.
Overlay chart comparing measured and modeled transistor I–V curves at 77 K.

paper_title: Surrogate-Assisted Compact-Model Extraction for SKY130 CMOS at 77 K
paper_authors: Aaron Wang, Olivia Gzamouranis, Vaibhav Lohia, Hershel Fei Xun Weiner, Olivia Seidel
